themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints in CD 402 spiked to 194 THIS WEEK, a 518% increase from the 31.4-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.6), signaling either sudden infrastructure failure or a reporting cascade tied to winter weather damage.
evidence: 194 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 31.4 weekly average (518% spike, z-score 9.6)
46 abandoned vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 23.2 weekly average (98% spike, z-score 4.58) — suggests street obstruction compounding pavement issues
Street sweeping complaints spiked to 5 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1900% increase, z-score 7.18) — pattern suggests debris accumulation tied to street condition
reporting_angles: Field inspection: photograph worst streets in Sunnyside/Woodside; identify geographic cluster (which blocks/avenues?)
Interview DOT: what triggered the spike? Winter pothole campaign response? Budget cuts? Deferred maintenance?
Resident impact: interview residents about commute hazards, bike accidents, or vehicle damage tied to street disrepair

themes_detail.label: Construction Site Safety Surge
themes_detail.summary: BEST/Site Safety complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a historical baseline of 0.1 complaints weekly (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69), coinciding with 605 active building permits filed in the past 90 days—suggesting inadequate site oversight during active construction.
evidence: 3 BEST/Site Safety complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
605 total DOB building permits filed in past 90 days (413 alterations, 102 new buildings) — highest construction activity level in dataset
Teen killed in garbage truck incident (Gothamist, 2026-03-30) in adjacent area — signals ongoing street safety risks during active construction/commercial vehicle operations
reporting_angles: Investigate which sites generated complaints: Are they the 102 new building projects or 413 alterations? Are they on major corridors (Queens Blvd, Astoria Blvd)?
Interview DOB inspectors: What violations are being cited? Inadequate sidewalk sheds? Unsecured equipment? Unsafe pedestrian pathways?
Street-level reporting: document construction sites with safety lapses; interview pedestrians and nearby residents about hazards

themes_detail.label: Rodent & Sanitation Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal (private property) complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score 6.35), while rodent complaints spiked to 11 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO from 3.2 weekly average (238% increase, z-score 5.57)—indicating a converging pest and sanitation crisis.
evidence: 3 unsanitary animal (private property) complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
11 rodent complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 3.2 weekly average (238% spike, z-score 5.57)
264 total unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days — 10th most-complained category; combined animal/rodent signals suggest source control failure
reporting_angles: Investigate waste management: Is illegal dumping or inadequate commercial waste disposal driving both rodent and animal complaints?
Interview DSNY and Health Department: Are rodent abatement programs active? Have baiting/trapping been deployed? What's the lag on response times?
Resident canvass: Ask residents about visible rodent activity, unsealed trash, or abandoned buildings harboring pests

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting & Street Disorder
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 3 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 0.1 weekly (2300% increase, z-score 8.69), while street/sidewalk noise complaints surged to 24 THIS WEEK from 10.4 weekly average (131% spike, z-score 3.94)—both signals of deteriorating public order and enforcement capacity.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
24 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.4 weekly average (131% increase, z-score 3.94)
827 total noise complaints over 90 days (residential) — suggests enforcement gaps allowing both visual and auditory disorder to accumulate
reporting_angles: Map illegal posting: Are complaints clustered near commercial corridors (Queens Blvd, Astoria Blvd) or residential zones?
Interview NYPD and Sanitation: What enforcement prioritization exists for illegal posting? Are graffiti/poster removal crews adequately staffed?
Assess quality-of-life decline: Interview residents about cumulative effects of unchecked noise and visual clutter on neighborhood perception
